prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1089; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A dated repair quote from before the policy start shows this same damage already existed.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a rear-end collision at a traffic signal. The policyholder's vehicle was struck from behind, and the claimant, who is not represented by counsel, reports neck and back pain following the impact.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and the statements from two independent witnesses. Both confirm the collision occurred as described and that the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time.

Entry 3: Photographs from the scene and the other driver's account match the reported impact. The rear damage to the vehicle is consistent with a collision of this type, and no earlier damage to this area is known from prior claims or records.

Entry 4: A repair estimate from before the policy start date lists damage to the same rear area of the vehicle. This conflicts with the assumption that the damage came from this collision and needs to be followed up with the repair shop.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant, who has added a few small details about the sequence of events. The core account has not changed from the first report.

Entry 6: The claimant's treatment record shows a usual course of care for a neck and back strain, with visits tapering off as symptoms improved. No prior injury to the same body area is known, and the reported injury is plausible for a crash of this severity.

Entry 7: The driver is a household member of the policyholder and qualifies for coverage under the policy terms. Recommend holding the file open pending review of the pre-policy repair estimate before any settlement offer is made.
